note: Screen 11a tables, 11/11b cards, 11c assembly. 8 MER (Athena payload + extras) and 6 real alternatives from Curiosity / Perseverance. mount = where it fits on THIS rover (mast, body, arm, deck). compat: 'yes' = built for MER · 'redesign' = real tool that needs a different arm/electronics · 'offgoal' = real tech that answers a different question.

requirements.text: Capture panoramic images of the Martian landscape.
Examine rocks and soil at close range.
Identify minerals that may have formed in water.
Analyze the chemical composition of rocks.
Expose fresh rock surfaces for analysis.

values_note: cost ($), mass (kg) and energy (%) on each instrument are SIMULATED GAME VALUES, not official NASA data. Packing an instrument in the kit adds its cost and mass to the HUD and draws its energy.

instruments.name: PANCAM
instruments.what: Two panoramic cameras that take detailed, multi-wavelength, 3-D panoramic pictures of the landscape around the rover.
instruments.role: Look over the terrain and find rocks worth a closer look.
instruments.mountText: On the mast, at about human eye height

instruments.name: MASTCAM-Z
instruments.what: Mast cameras with a zoom lens that take high-definition video, panoramic color and 3D images and magnify distant targets.
instruments.role: Great panoramas, but designed for a newer, bigger rover.
instruments.compatText: Excellent images, but not a direct MER part: it needs a redesign of the mast electronics.

instruments.name: MICROSCOPIC IMAGER
instruments.what: Extreme close-up black-and-white views of rocks and soils, giving context for the minerals and elements.
instruments.role: See the texture of a rock up close.
instruments.mountText: On the turret at the end of the robotic arm
instruments.compatText: Built for this rover's arm turret.

instruments.name: MAHLI
instruments.what: Mars Hand Lens Imager: microscopic imaging of minerals, textures and structures at scales smaller than the width of a human hair.
instruments.role: Even closer views, but built for Curiosity's arm.
instruments.mountText: On the turret at the end of the robotic arm (Curiosity's)
instruments.compatText: Great close-ups, but it needs Curiosity's arm and electronics.

instruments.name: MINI-TES
instruments.what: Miniature Thermal Emission Spectrometer: measures the infrared light (heat) given off by minerals. It is tuned to look for minerals formed in water.
instruments.role: Spot water minerals from far away.
instruments.mountText: In the body, looking out through the mast

instruments.name: CHEMIN
instruments.what: Chemistry and Mineralogy instrument: uses X-rays to identify and measure the minerals in powdered rock or soil delivered by the arm.
instruments.role: Very precise minerals, but it needs a drill and a sample inlet.
instruments.mountText: Inside the rover body (needs a drill to feed it powder)
instruments.compatText: Excellent mineralogy, but MER had no drill to feed it powdered samples.

instruments.name: MOSSBAUER
instruments.what: Mössbauer Spectrometer: determines the makeup and quantities of iron-bearing minerals in rocks and soils.
instruments.mountText: On the turret at the end of the robotic arm
instruments.compatText: Built for this rover's arm turret.

instruments.name: APXS
instruments.what: Alpha Particle X-Ray Spectrometer: determines the chemical elements that make up rocks and soils.
instruments.role: Measure the chemistry of a rock.
instruments.mountText: On the turret at the end of the robotic arm
instruments.compatText: Built for this rover's arm turret.

instruments.name: PIXL
instruments.what: Planetary Instrument for X-ray Lithochemistry: measures the chemical makeup of rocks at a very fine scale.
instruments.role: Very useful for chemistry, but built for a newer rover.
instruments.mountText: On the arm (needs a different arm and electronics)
instruments.compatText: Excellent science, but not a direct MER part: it needs specific integration with the arm and other systems.

instruments.name: ROCK ABRASION TOOL
instruments.what: The RAT's rotating grinding teeth gnaw into the surface of a rock to reveal fresh mineral surfaces for the other instruments.
instruments.role: Grind away the dusty skin of a rock.
instruments.mountText: On the turret at the end of the robotic arm
instruments.compatText: Built for this rover's arm turret.

instruments.name: MAGNET ARRAY
instruments.what: Magnets that collect airborne dust so the other instruments can study what it is made of.
instruments.mountText: On the rover deck and front (and on the RAT)

instruments.name: MEDA
instruments.what: Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzer: measures weather and monitors dust with sensors on the rover.
instruments.role: Real weather station, but it does not study ancient water in rocks.
instruments.mountText: Sensors on the mast and deck (Perseverance's)
instruments.compatText: Real technology, but it answers a different question (weather today, not ancient water).

instruments.name: CALIBRATION TARGETS
instruments.what: Objects with known properties (like the Pancam sundial) used as reference points to fine-tune the instruments.

instruments.name: MOXIE
instruments.what: A technology experiment that makes oxygen from the carbon dioxide in Mars's thin atmosphere.
instruments.role: Real tech that makes oxygen, but it does not study ancient water.
instruments.compatText: Amazing technology for future explorers, but it answers a different question.
